oneSentenceSummary: This paper introduces a novel framework that extracts four interpretable 'narrative factors' from 94 US labour market indicators to resolve conflicting signals, revealing that the post-pandemic soft landing was driven by both cooling demand and an unusual decline in short-run labour supply.
originalTitle: Making sense of conflicting labour market signals
summary: This VoxEU column addresses the challenge of interpreting conflicting US labour market signals—where payroll growth slows, vacancies decline, but unemployment remains low and wage growth persists. The authors propose a framework that uses principal components analysis on 94 monthly and quarterly time series (1960–2026) and rotates them with sign restrictions from textbook models to produce four 'narrative factors': labour demand, long-run labour supply, short-run labour supply, and matching efficiency. The framework formalizes the narratives policymakers already use implicitly. A key finding is that the post-pandemic soft landing was not solely a demand-side story; a simultaneous contraction in short-run labour supply suppressed the unemployment rate by about 0.75 percentage points and reduced monthly payroll growth by roughly 90,000 jobs. This explains the paradox of households finding it harder to get jobs while firms struggle to fill vacancies. The column emphasizes that no single indicator should be interpreted in isolation and provides a systematic method for organizing noisy, real-time data into coherent economic narratives.
title: Making sense of conflicting labour market signals
